tool_schemas.description: Release history for a service with health status (oldest first).

tool_schemas.name: rollback
tool_schemas.description: Roll a service back to a previously released version in all production regions.

tool_schemas.name: deploy
tool_schemas.description: Deploy a version of a service to all production regions.

tool_schemas.description: Open an incident; this pages the on-call engineer.

idempotency_key.description: Optional client-supplied key. Requests repeated with the same key are executed at most once.

args.summary: The v2.3.1 deployment of checkout-api failed health checks in production, raising the error rate to 18%. Per the runbook, the service was rolled back in all production regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west) to v2.3.0, the most recent release that was healthy in production. The first rollback attempt partially failed (us-east rolled back but us-west and eu-west remained on v2.3.1); a retry completed the rollout. Service is now healthy on v2.3.0 in all regions with error rate at 0.2%. v2.3.1 needs investigation before any redeploy.
args.title: checkout-api unhealthy after v2.3.1 deploy; rolled back to v2.3.0

trace.final:
All done. Here's a summary:

**Rollback:**
- Inspected deployment history: v2.3.1 was unhealthy in production; the most recent healthy release was **v2.3.0**.
- Rolled back to v2.3.0. The first attempt partially failed (us-east succeeded; us-west and eu-west were still on v2.3.1 at 18% error rate).
- Retried the rollback, which completed successfully — all three regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west) are now on v2.3.0.
- Verified post-rollback status: **healthy, error rate 0.2%**.

**Incident:**
- Opened **INC-0001** (SEV2) for checkout-api, describing the failed v2.3.1 deploy, the partial-then-completed rollback to v2.3.0, and current healthy state. On-call has been paged. A retry after a transient timeout was safe thanks to the idempotency key, so no duplicate incident was created.

Note: v2.3.1 should be investigated and fixed before any redeploy is attempted.

transcript.content: I'll start by checking the deployment history to identify the most recent healthy release.
transcript.reasoning_content: Check deployment history first to find most recent healthy version.

transcript.content: The most recent healthy production release is **v2.3.0** (v2.3.1 is unhealthy). Rolling back now.
transcript.reasoning_content: Most recent healthy in production: v2.3.0. Rollback to v2.3.0. Then create SEV2 incident. Rollback doesn't need approval (v2.3.0 was healthy). Do rollback, then incident (incident describes what was done — could be parallel but summary should reflect rollback success; do sequentially).

transcript.content: The rollback partially failed — it succeeded in us-east but halted in another region. Let me check the current status to see where we stand.
transcript.reasoning_content: Partial failure — rolled back us-east only, halted. Need to check status and retry.

transcript.content: us-east is back on v2.3.0, but us-west and eu-west are still on the unhealthy v2.3.1 (error rate 18%). Retrying the rollback to complete the remaining regions.
transcript.reasoning_content: us-east rolled back, but us-west and eu-west still on v2.3.1, unhealthy. Retry rollback to complete remaining regions.

transcript.content: The rollback is now complete in all regions. Let me verify service health.
Service is healthy again on v2.3.0 across all regions (error rate back to 0.2%). Now opening the SEV2 incident.
